documents.title: Hematology-oncology end-of-treatment note, 12/18/2020
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER, HEMATOLOGY-ONCOLOGY — Follow-up, 12/18/2020
Waldenström macroglobulinemia, IgM lambda, MYD88 L265P, presented with hyperviscosity. Status after plasma exchange (06/2020) and six cycles of bendamustine-rituximab completed in November.
Today: feels stronger, no headaches or visual symptoms. Persistent mild tingling in the feet.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics, iodinated contrast.
Labs: IgM 1,320 mg/dL (from 4,850); hemoglobin 12.1.
Assessment: Partial response.
Plan: Observation, no maintenance therapy. Labs and visit every 3 months. Okay for COVID vaccination when available.
Hematology-oncology physician

documents.title: Follow-up after WM treatment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since chemo ended. Energy better. Both COVID vaccines done. Vision fine since cataract surgery. Feet still tingle. Neck and gait stable; uses cane outdoors. Pain clinic unchanged.
Exam: vitals as charted. Color better. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: reduced light touch distally, skin intact.
A/P: WM in partial response, observation by cancer center. Labs today for diabetes, kidneys, lipids and blood count. Continue everything.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb up to 12.6. Total protein now 7.4, albumin 3.8. Kidney function back at his usual. A1c and lipids in his usual range. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Leg swelling and fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For about three months: more and more tired, both legs swelling, needs two pillows to breathe at night, and the urine looks foamy. Lost weight without trying, belt two notches tighter. No chest pain, no fever.
O: Weight 84 kg, down from 92 last year. BP as charted. JVP hard to assess. Bibasilar breath sounds slightly reduced. Pitting edema both legs to mid-shin. Dipstick protein 3+.
A/P: New heavy proteinuria with edema, orthopnea and weight loss in a man with WM after treatment: concern for a paraprotein-related kidney problem such as amyloid, or heart involvement. BMP and urine albumin/creatinine today. Called the cancer center: his 6/4 visit will be used for the workup (24-hour urine, echo, light chains). Leg elevation, low-salt diet. ED if breathing worsens.

documents.title: BMP and urine albumin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.9 (from about 1.4). Urine albumin/creatinine 3,400 mg/g. Forwarded to hematology-oncology. Potassium fine.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Pharmacy call: new outside prescriptions
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacist called to check an interaction alert: pt filled furosemide 40 mg daily and acyclovir 400 mg twice daily on 6/8 from the cancer center. They flagged the sulfa allergy with furosemide; he has taken HCTZ for years without a reaction, and the hives were from a sulfa antibiotic. Okay to dispense. No note from the cancer center yet. Added both as outside prescriptions. Request sent for the 6/4 note.

documents.title: Wife update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wife Lorraine called. The cancer center told them the swelling and kidney protein are from amyloidosis (AL type) related to his blood disorder, found on a fat biopsy, and that the heart is involved. He starts a new treatment this week (weekly injections plus pills on infusion days). Water pill helping, legs down some. Answered questions; will review the full letter when it arrives. She's scared. Offered a visit for both of them anytime.

reports.text:
Indication: AL amyloidosis evaluation, orthopnea, edema.
Left ventricle: normal cavity size. Increased wall thickness, concentric. Systolic function preserved, LVEF estimated 55%. Diastolic assessment: mitral inflow and tissue velocity measurements indicate a restrictive filling pattern.
Right ventricle: normal size, wall thickened, function preserved.
Atria: normal size.
Valves: structurally normal aortic and mitral valves.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Increased ventricular wall thickness with normal chamber size and restrictive filling, consistent with infiltrative cardiomyopathy in the setting of AL amyloidosis.

reports.text: Liver enlarged, measuring 19.5 cm craniocaudal at the midclavicular line, homogeneous echotexture, no focal lesion. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation. Gallbladder normal. Pancreas partly obscured. Spleen normal size. Kidneys normal size without hydronephrosis. No ascites.

documents.title: Hematology-oncology consultation, 06/04/2021 (received 07/19)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER, HEMATOLOGY-ONCOLOGY — Follow-up and new diagnosis, 06/04/2021
(Received by fax 07/19/2021 after two requests.)

Interval: Waldenström macroglobulinemia on observation after bendamustine-rituximab. Three months of progressive fatigue, swelling of both legs, weight loss without trying, orthopnea, and frothy urine. PCP's 5/24 labs reviewed.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, morphine ER 60 mg BID, morphine IR 15 mg prn, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, HCTZ, metformin.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (hives), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Vitals: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 18.
Exam: Low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur. Striking purpura around both eyes. Pitting edema to the knees bilaterally.

Labs: albumin 2.8, creatinine 1.9, 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g, total cholesterol 260. Liver tests mildly elevated: alkaline phosphatase 196, AST 44, ALT 39. Free lambda light chain 212 mg/L, free kappa 15.4 mg/L. NT-proBNP 2,870 pg/mL.
Abdominal fat pad aspirate: amyloid deposits present; typed as AL lambda.
Echo and abdominal ultrasound: reports attached.

Assessment: AL (lambda) amyloidosis with kidney (nephrotic-range proteinuria), heart and liver involvement, arising from his lymphoplasmacytic clone.
Plan:
- Bortezomib (subcutaneous weekly), dexamethasone and rituximab, 28-day cycles x6, starting this month.
- Acyclovir 400 mg twice daily for zoster prophylaxis during bortezomib.
- Furosemide 40 mg daily for edema; daily weights, low-sodium diet.
- Dexamethasone will raise his sugars; please follow glucose.
Hematology-oncology physician

documents.title: Follow-up: AL amyloidosis, diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife and daughter. Cancer center letter (6/4) finally received 7/19; reviewed with them today. Two cycles of bortezomib/dex/rituximab done. Swelling better on furosemide, sleeping on one pillow. Sugars run higher on dexamethasone days (200s), otherwise 140s. Tingling in feet the same.
Exam: vitals as charted. Periorbital bruising fading. Diastolic murmur as described by oncology, low-pitched. Trace ankle edema. Lungs clear.
A/P:
1. AL amyloidosis on treatment, cancer center managing.
2. T2DM: A1c today, expect higher with steroids. Continue metformin for now; will revisit if creatinine climbs further.
3. HTN/CKD: BMP for potassium and creatinine on furosemide + HCTZ + lisinopril.
Daughter Kristen added to HIPAA release; she will use the portal for him.

documents.title: Hematology-oncology follow-up, 01/14/2022
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER — Follow-up, 01/14/2022
AL lambda amyloidosis (kidney, heart, liver) arising from Waldenström macroglobulinemia. Completed six cycles of bortezomib, dexamethasone and rituximab in November 2021.
Symptoms: edema much improved, orthopnea resolved; mild neuropathy in feet, unchanged.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics, iodinated contrast.
Labs: free lambda light chain 24 mg/L (from 212); 24-hour urine protein 2.2 g (from 4.5); NT-proBNP 1,950 pg/mL (from 2,870).
Assessment: Very good partial hematologic response with early organ response.
Plan: Observation, labs and visit every 3-4 months. Continue furosemide 40 mg daily. Continue acyclovir until March, then stop.
Hematology-oncology physician

orders.reason: progressive memory loss, gait instability, urinary incontinence

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Memory, gait and continence
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter Kristen. Since about spring: forgetting conversations and appointments, repeating questions, walking more unsteady (shuffling, 'feet stuck'), and leaking urine before reaching the bathroom. He used to manage his own pills and bills; now wife and daughter help with dressing, bathing and medicines. He minimizes, says he's 'just slower.' No falls with injury. No fever, no new medicines.
Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, recall 1/3 at 5 minutes, clock drawing disorganized. Gait slow, wide-based, short steps; turns in several steps. Strength in legs full. Reflexes as before.
A/P: Triad of cognitive decline, gait change and urinary incontinence over ~6 months. Differential includes normal pressure hydrocephalus, vascular disease (prior TIA), progression of cervical myelopathy, medication effect (opioids). B12, TSH, BMP and UA today. Neurology referral, prior neurologist's office. Fall safety, supervised meds. Daughter to keep a list of episodes.

documents.title: Cognitive workup labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: B12, TSH, sodium and calcium normal. UA without infection. Neurology appointment 11/21.

reports.text:
Indication: memory loss, gait instability, incontinence.
Technique: Noncontrast axial CT of the head.
Findings: Lateral and third ventricles are enlarged out of proportion to the cortical sulci, which are normal in size. No acute hemorrhage, mass, or territorial infarct. No extra-axial collection. Postoperative change of the left lens.
reports.conclusion: Ventriculomegaly with normal-sized sulci. Clinical correlation for normal pressure hydrocephalus.

documents.title: Neurology consultation, 11/21/2022
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY — Consultation, 11/21/2022
Seen with his daughter for six months of worsening memory, unsteady walking and urinary incontinence; previously independent, he now needs help with daily activities. Known to us for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (nonoperative). Also Waldenström macroglobulinemia and AL amyloidosis.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, tamsulosin, morphine ER and IR, atorvastatin, aspirin, furosemide.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics, iodinated contrast.
Exam: Wide-based gait with feet that seem stuck to the floor; cannot do tandem walking. No weakness. Sensation intact. MMSE 24/30.
CT head without contrast today: large ventricles with normal sulci (report attached).
Impression: Normal pressure hydrocephalus with mild cognitive impairment.
Plan: High-volume lumbar tap test with timed walking before and after; decide on shunt referral based on the response.
Neurologist

documents.title: Lumbar tap test, 01/17/2023
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY — Procedure and follow-up note
Procedure (01/17/2023): High-volume lumbar puncture, L3-4, lateral decubitus, sterile technique, no complications. Aspirin not held. Opening pressure 13 cm H2O. 35 mL clear CSF removed.
Assessment: 10-meter walk 21 seconds before, 18 seconds at 3 hours after. MMSE unchanged. Daughter felt he walked 'a little lighter' that afternoon only.
Impression: Modest response. Given AL amyloidosis with cardiac involvement, frailty and the small improvement, we and the family agreed not to pursue shunt surgery.
Plan: Physical therapy for gait and balance; walker for distances; follow up in neurology clinic in a year or sooner for change.
Neurologist

documents.title: Physical therapy evaluation

OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY — Initial evaluation, 02/14/2023
Referral: neurology, gait instability with NPH and cervical myelopathy.
Findings: slow, wide-based, shuffling gait; difficulty turning; tandem not possible; sit-to-stand needs arms. Uses cane; fitted for rolling walker today.
Plan: 2x/week for 8 weeks: gait training, balance, lower-extremity strengthening, home safety.
Physical therapist

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit and advance care planning
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife and daughter. Needs help with bathing and medicines; walks with walker. Memory about the same as last winter per family. PHQ-9 4.
Advance care planning (about 30 min): Dennis able to take part and states his wishes clearly. He names his wife Lorraine as health care proxy, daughter as alternate; form signed and scanned. What matters to him: staying at home, being with family, not being kept alive on machines if he could not recognize them. Family will continue the conversation; we will revisit yearly.
Exam: as charted.
Vaccines: flu and updated COVID next month here.

Daughter brought him. She feels his memory is slipping more this fall, harder to plan anything, sometimes confused in the evening. He still drives to the corner store on his own, which worries her. Neurology follow-up already set for January.
Exam: vitals as charted; walker gait.
